topIssues.title: kona/protocol: brotli decoder (brotli-decompressor) is more lenient than op-node (andybalholm) — accepts malformed channels op-node rejects
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Differential testing of the two brotli decoders used in OP Stack derivation — `brotli-decompressor` 5.0.1 (kona, [`decompress_brotli`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/44e40ba521c9ec2ad02f3ed7db3e79055afa9877/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs#L19-L90)) vs `andybalholm/brotli` v1.1.0 (op-node, [`BatchReader`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/44e40ba521c9ec2ad02f3ed7db3e79055afa9877/op-node/rollup/derive/channel.go#L174-L219)) — shows the two disagree on brotli **validity**. The consensus-relevant direction: **kona's decoder accepts malformed channels that op-node rejects.** kona would then RLP-decode batches op-node discards. If any such batch is valid, kona advances the safe chain where op-node does not → consensus split. This is the mirror image of #20666 (which worried about the opposite direction — that one turns out to be structurally impossible for the current eager decoder).

This is the *residual* decoder gap behind [protocol-team#84 (strict channel decompression)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/84): strict semantics remove the unbounded partial-output surface but leave this validity-boundary disagreement, which needs decoder conformance work.

## Evidence

Over 70,526 adversarial streams (corruptions + truncations + fuzz), classifying each by whether the decoder reaches a *clean* end-of-stream:

| | count |
|---|---|
| both decoders accept | 58,695 |
| …of which **byte-length mismatch** | **0** |
| both reject | 5,941 |
| **kona accepts, op-node rejects** (kona too lenient) | **242** |
| kona rejects, op-node accepts (op-node too lenient) | 5,648 |

Key facts:
- **Accepted streams never diverge** (0 length mismatches) — valid brotli is deterministic. All divergence is at the accept/reject boundary.
- The 242 kona-too-lenient cases collapse to two root causes: `BLOCK_LENGTH_1/2` (98) and `excessive input` (144).

## Root cause 1 — `BLOCK_LENGTH` (confirmed, fix in hand)

`brotli-decompressor`'s `BROTLI_STATE_METABLOCK_DONE` handler is **missing the `meta_block_remaining_len < 0` check** that andybalholm ([decode.go#L2464-L2468](https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/blob/v1.1.0/decode.go#L2464-L2468)) and the C reference enforce. When a metablock's insert-copy commands overshoot the declared MLEN, `meta_block_remaining_len` goes negative; the command loop breaks to `METABLOCK_DONE`, which runs cleanup and proceeds to `SUCCESS` without validating. andybalholm rejects with `BLOCK_LENGTH_2`.

Confirmed by red/green in an isolated copy of the crate: unpatched accepts **98/98** of the malformed streams; with a 5-line check added it accepts **0/98** (matching andybalholm), and all valid streams still decode:

```diff
         BrotliRunningState::BROTLI_STATE_METABLOCK_DONE => {
+          if (s.meta_block_remaining_len < 0) {
+            result = BrotliDecoderErrorCode::BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_LENGTH_2;
+            break;
+          }
           s.BrotliStateCleanupAfterMetablock();
```

This is the **same class** as the PADDING_2 fix ([dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44](https://github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor/pull/44)) — a missing end-of-metablock validation in the very same state handler. It needs an **upstream fix in `brotli-decompressor`**, then a version bump here (like #21505 did for PADDING_2).

## Root cause 2 — `excessive input` (trailing bytes)

andybalholm rejects a stream with bytes remaining after the final metablock (`excessive input`); `brotli-decompressor` stops at the ISLAST metablock and returns success, ignoring the trailing bytes. **Fixable at the kona wrapper** by requiring the input reader to be fully consumed — the `decompress_brotli_strict` "reader fully consumed" check floated in #20666 (the one sound idea there). Under strict semantics this is the natural rule: a channel with trailing garbage is invalid.

## Reverse direction (for completeness)

The 5,648 "op-node accepts, kona rejects" cases are **89% truncations**: andybalholm treats a truncated stream as clean (returns partial output, nil error), while `brotli-decompressor` correctly rejects it (RFC 7932: a truncated stream is invalid). Here **andybalholm** is the lenient/non-conformant side. This direction also causes divergence (op-node ahead) and needs an op-node-side decision, since op-node is the incumbent.

## Relationship to strict decompression (protocol-team#84)

Strict semantics are the right foundation and should land regardless — they guarantee accepted channels produce identical output and delete the entire best-effort partial-output surface. But strict is **necessary, not sufficient**: it reduces the problem from "identical partial bytes on every malformed stream" (implementation-defined, ~impossible) to "agree on validity" (a spec-defined boolean) — and the decoders still disagree on that boolean. Closing it is the bounded conformance work below.

## Proposed work

- [ ] Upstream `brotli-decompressor`: add the `BLOCK_LENGTH_2` check to `METABLOCK_DONE` (patch above; sibling to #44) — PR up at dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#47; then bump the pin here once it releases.
- [ ] kona wrapper: require the input reader fully consumed → rejects `excessive input` — **#84-gated; do NOT land standalone.** Under today's best-effort rule op-node already keeps the valid-portion batches from an `excessive input` channel (its "excessive input" error routes through the same `NextChannel` + keep-partial path as `io.EOF`), and kona agrees (it ignores the trailing bytes and decodes the same batches). Adding this check now would make kona drop those batches (0 for the whole channel, via `decompress_brotli(...)?`) → a *new* kona-too-strict divergence. It reaches parity only once #84 makes op-node reject the whole channel too. (Same #84-gating applies to every "make the decoder stricter" step here, incl. the dropbox#47 `BLOCK_LENGTH` bump: today both clients keep partial batches and agree; tightening one side alone breaks that.)
- [x] op-node/andybalholm truncation direction — bumped op-node to andybalholm v1.2.2 (#21799, **merged**). The decoder now rejects truncated streams per RFC 7932 §9.3, matching the C reference and kona. The bump is behaviorally inert on its own (verified byte-identical batch output v1.1.0 vs v1.2.2); it provides the `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` signal that the strict-decompression rule handling (below) acts on.
- [ ] Land protocol-team#84 (strict decompression) as the foundational rule change — includes the op-node rule handling that acts on the new `ErrUnexpectedEOF` signal to reject truncated channels, plus kona going strict.
- [ ] Gate a Go↔Rust differential *validity* fuzzer in CI (now feasible — it compares a boolean, not byte sequences).

## Methodology

Differential harness: kona's `brotli-decompressor` decode status vs `andybalholm/brotli` `io.ReadAll` over a shared corpus (corruptions of valid streams, truncations, random fuzz). Root cause confirmed by red/green against an isolated copy of `brotli-decompressor` 5.0.1. Harnesses and the 98 `BLOCK_LENGTH` reproducers are available on request.

## References

- #20666 — proposed the opposite-direction fix (refuted; the current eager decoder can't lag op-node)
- #19333 / #20598 / #20004 — original brotli divergence investigation and Bug 1/Bug 2 fixes
- #21505 — the PADDING_2 bump (brotli-decompressor 5.0.1)
- [dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44](https://github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor/pull/44) — PADDING_2 fix (same bug class)
- [protocol-team#84](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/84) — strict channel decompression

topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §1, §2, §3, §4, §5 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Once the `op-core/*` packages exist, swap all relevant call-sites in the Go services so they stop reaching into op-geth internals. No behaviour change — just imports and types.

## Scope

### DepositTx construction / decoding

Replace the `types.NewTx(&types.DepositTx{...}).MarshalBinary()` pattern throughout op-node with `optypes.DepositTx{...}.MarshalBinary()` — the `*types.Transaction` wrapper is eliminated, we go straight from struct to `[]byte`. Files to edit:
- `op-node/rollup/derive/deposits.go`, `deposit_log.go`, `parse_upgrade_transactions.go`
- `op-node/rollup/derive/*_upgrade_transactions.go` (Ecotone, Fjord, Holocene, Isthmus, Jovian, Interop, Karst)
- `op-node/rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go`

`UnmarshalDepositLogEvent` returns `*optypes.DepositTx`.

### Transaction methods → helpers

- `tx.IsDepositTx()` → `optypes.IsDepositTx(tx)`
- `tx.SourceHash()` / `tx.Mint()` / `tx.IsSystemTx()` → decode raw bytes via `optypes.UnmarshalDepositTx` and read fields, or use helpers from #20262.
- `tx.From()` on a deposit tx (single call site in `op-node/rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go:105`) → same pattern.
- `tx.RollupCostData()` → `opfees.TxRollupCostData(tx)`.

### Receipt (`*optypes.Receipt`) in `op-service/txinclude`

- `op-service/txinclude/interfaces.go` `EL.TransactionReceipt` return type → `*optypes.Receipt`.
- `op-service/txinclude/persistent.go`, `monitor.go`, `txbudget.go`: update references.
- Replace inline operator-fee math in `txbudget.go` and `isthmus_cost_oracle.go` with `opfees.OperatorCost(gasUsed, scalar, constant)`.
- Replace `types.NewL1CostFuncFjord` with `opfees.NewL1CostFuncFjord`.

### `OptimismConfig` and `ChainConfig`

- `rollup.Config.ChainOpConfig *params.OptimismConfig` → `*opparams.OptimismConfig`.
- `rollup.Config` gets any missing hardfork timestamp fields (KarstTime, InteropTime if not already present).
- `op-service/eth/BlockAsPayload` and `BlockAsPayloadEnv`: replace `config *params.ChainConfig` parameter with a local `HardforkConfig` interface (`IsCanyon(uint64) bool`, `IsIsthmus(uint64) bool`). Callers pass `rollup.Config` directly.

### EIP-1559 helpers

- `op-node/rollup/derive/payload_util.go`, `rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go`, `rollup/attributes/engine_consolidate.go`: switch imports from `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/consensus/misc/eip1559` to `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/eip1559`.

### Superchain loader

- `op-service/superutil/` is deleted (the function moved to `op-core/superchain` in #20259).
- `op-node/rollup/superchain.go`, `op-node/chaincfg/chains.go`: switch imports from `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/superchain` to `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/superchain`.

## Dependencies

Blocked on: #20260 (`op-core/params`), #20261 (`op-core/fees`), #20262 (`op-core/types`), #20259 (`op-core/superchain` + `op-core/eip1559`).

topPRs.title: test: reproduce #21663 NUT bundle drift via L2DevFeatureFlags version bump
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Do not merge — diagnostic experiment for the CI failures in ethereum-optimism/optimism#21663.

**What this shows:** the karst/lagoon NUT activation failures come from the **semver downgrade guard** in `L2ContractsManagerUtils.upgradeTo` (reverts `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` when the installed proxy version > the version the bundle installs), combined with a test-fixture gap: **L2DevFeatureFlags is not captured in any pre-fork state file**, so the NUT activation test rebuilds it from HEAD instead of the fork era.

- Before: HEAD L2DevFeatureFlags = 1.0.0, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.0,1.0.0)=false` → pass.
- After the bump: HEAD = 1.0.1, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.1,1.0.0)=true` → downgrade → revert.

Commits:
1. bump L2DevFeatureFlags semver 1.0.0 → 1.0.1
2. comment-only touch to the NUT test file (contracts-only changes don't set `rust_changes_detected`, so the NUT test would be skipped — a CI gap in its own right)
3. regenerate `current-upgrade-bundle.json`
4. regenerate `semver-lock.json`
5. bump the version unit test to 1.0.1 + re-snapshot the **lagoon** bundle (karst left immutable)

Expected CI after commit 5: snapshot checks + version test green; **lagoon** NUT/interop green (bundle now installs 1.0.1, matching HEAD); **karst** NUT still red (its immutable bundle installs 1.0.0 while the test's HEAD genesis has 1.0.1). Note: `nut-provenance-verify lagoon` will fail because the lock commit is the develop merge-base, which predates the change.

topPRs.title: op-script-engine: Rust forge-script executor + Go client and parity gates
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Rust `op-script-engine` crate + Go client and byte-parity gates — the base of the op-geth-decoupling script-engine stack (epic #20257 §16). **Additive: no production code selects this engine yet.**

Stack (each stacked on the previous):
1. **this PR** — engine crate, `rustengine` client, parity gates
2. non-forked op-deployer routing + engine default (follows)
3. fork-mode routing + boundary deletion (follows)

### Contents
- **`rust/op-script-engine`** — revm-based re-implementation of the `op-chain-ops/script` EVM host: a cheatcode + console `Inspector`, prank/broadcast capture, forge-artifact loader, state dump, the OPCM `RunScript*` input/output-precompile mechanism, and an RPC-backed fork mode. Served over a UDS JSON-RPC transport (reth-ipc + jsonrpsee).
- **`op-chain-ops/script/rustengine`** — Go client plus A/B parity tests that drive both the Go host and this engine and assert **byte-identical** output: state-dump + broadcast (incl. `gasUsed`), OPCM `RunScriptSingle`/`Void`, and forked `SetDisputeGameImpl` over a hermetic recorded-RPC fixture.
- **Additive helpers** the parity path needs: `script.Precompile` snapshot reflection, `script.Host.ExportDiff`, and a `forking.AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref fix. `go-tests` provisions the workspace-built binary so the gates run in CI.

### Gates (local)
- `cargo test -p op-script-engine` — 16/16
- `cargo clippy -p op-script-engine --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; nightly `fmt` clean
- `go test ./op-chain-ops/script/rustengine/` — parity / OPCM / forked / isolated-fork all pass
- base goldens (`TestScriptStateDump|TestScriptBroadcast`) and `./op-chain-ops/script/forking/` unchanged-green

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Review batch applied
Crate hardening (all byte-parity re-validated): contained worker-thread panics (`catch_unwind`); standard precompiles `0x01..=0x0a` no longer framed/broadcast-captured (matches the Go host, which frames only bytecode-bearing targets); `tx.chain_id: None` on raw calls (matches geth's `EVM.Call`, fixes a stale-id case after `vm.chainId`); host setters record into the fork diff when forked; documented that `isolate_broadcast`'s `transaction_id` bump also re-baselines SSTORE originals (revm's cold-slot reset == geth `Finalise(true)`).

Go client hardening: stderr drain uses `bufio.Reader` (no 64KiB line-cap hang); Linux `Pdeathsig=SIGKILL` so a hard-killed test can't leak engines. Test rigor: `TestMain`→`ProvisionTestBinary` + a `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE` guard so the byte-parity gate can't silently skip; a targeted `AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref regression test; non-vacuity guards on the parity subtests.

**Two flagged potential divergences investigated — both non-divergences:** the implemented cheatcode set is complete for the OPCM-routed scripts (env*/toString/parseJson/file-IO are used only by the legacy forge scripts, never routed; verified by the passing full-suite A/B gates), and the isolated-broadcast SSTORE-original re-baseline is handled by revm (source-confirmed).

**One real divergence found — access control:** enforcing Go's cheatcode access control naively breaks byte parity, because the routed deploy scripts deploy helper contracts that call cheatcodes and rely on Go's transitive auto-grant-on-deploy. Left **unenforced** (the current byte-parity-correct behavior, documented in `cheatcodes.rs`); correct enforcement needs the auto-grant replicated and is a dedicated follow-up.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: continue prepared chain deployments
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `op-deployer continue` for prepared deployments. `prepare` now snapshots its canonical intent, predicted addresses, deployer, OPCM, anchor timing, and contract artifact digests. `continue` uses that snapshot as its authority and rejects drift before execution.

All pending chains are simulated and verified before any transaction. Each send rechecks the anchor and deployer nonce, checkpoints the chain only after a canonical receipt, and verifies live configuration from one L1 block.

Retries reconcile complete deployments, reject partial deployments, and redeploy a checkpointed chain only when its deployment disappeared while the prepared anchor remains valid.

**Tests**

Covers prepared-input and artifact drift, all-chain preflight, broadcast guards, exact configuration checks, retries, reconciliation, reorg recovery, the full workflow, and the CLI.

**Additional context**

Stacked on #21897. The starting anchor proposal and prestate remain in chain state because they are derived after address prediction. Other continuation inputs cannot silently diverge from the prediction, including across retries after chain state is normalized.

Across multiple chains, independent L1 transactions cannot be atomic. A later failure leaves completed chains checkpointed for retry.

**Metadata**

Closes #21669
